title.zh: 模型变了，Pi 需要跟着改变吗？
title.en: When models change, should Pi change too?

sourceText: Welcome to our Monday Meditations. In which @badlogicgames and @mitsuhiko are talking about things that might or might not need to change in Pi given the changes in models.

zh.title: 模型转向 Bash，原有交互也要调整
zh.text: 两人观察到新模型更倾向于通过 Bash 和 Python 修改文件，而不是调用专门的编辑工具。这会影响错误反馈、diff 展示，以及人对执行过程的可见性。

zh.title: 什么时候值得看执行记录
zh.text: 普通编码任务中，两人更多在完成后用编辑器审查结果；涉及 CI、远程服务或边讨论边探索时，过程记录仍然重要。不同用途需要不同的呈现方式。

zh.title: 快照与 diff 并没有统一答案
zh.text: 他们讨论用独立 Git 索引合成修改记录的方案，也指出跨目录操作、性能和多一层状态的成本。小提交和更好的 diff 工具仍是重要方向。

zh.title: 顺应模型行为，同时重新设计体验
zh.text: Pi 原有界面接近模型事件的直接呈现。两人提出通过工具参数中的简短描述、额外摘要等方式改善可读性，并把这些办法视为需要实验的方向。

zh.title: 安全边界不能只依赖工具分类
zh.text: 当模型把操作集中到 Bash 或代码执行中，基于单个工具的审批会失去部分意义。Mario 质疑缺乏完整上下文的二次模型判断，更强调沙箱约束。

zh.title: MCP 与 code mode 需要结构化输出
zh.text: 两人探讨 MCP 的鉴权价值以及代码编排需要的数据形态。Armin 分享 Radius 使用任务相关 OpenAPI schema 的经验，并认为面向代码调用的服务应提供结构化结果。

zh.title: 仍需评估模型差异与新用途
zh.text: 他们认为 MCP 加 code mode 有潜力，但不同模型的实现、能力及本地模型支持仍需测试。Armin 还提出用代码定义工作流，再由 Jev 反复选择路径的用途。

en.title: Bash-oriented models change the interaction
en.text: They observe newer models preferring Bash and Python over dedicated edit tools, affecting error feedback, diff presentation and the user’s visibility into execution.

en.title: When the execution transcript matters
en.text: For routine coding, both often inspect the finished changes in an editor. Process visibility still matters for CI, remote services and conversations that alternate between exploration and discussion.

en.title: Snapshots and diffs involve tradeoffs
en.text: They discuss synthesizing diffs through a separate Git index, including costs around cross-directory work, performance and additional state. Small commits and better diff tools remain valuable.

en.title: Follow model behavior while rethinking the interface
en.text: Pi’s interface has closely reflected model events. They propose experiments such as short descriptions in tool arguments and additional summaries to make increasingly complex calls easier to follow.

en.title: Tool categories alone cannot define the safety boundary
en.text: As operations move into Bash and code execution, approvals based on individual tool types lose some usefulness. Mario questions secondary-model judgments without full context and emphasizes sandbox constraints.

en.title: MCP and code mode need structured results
en.text: They discuss MCP’s authentication role and the data needed for code orchestration. Armin describes task-relevant OpenAPI schemas in Radius and argues for structured results from services intended for programmatic use.

en.title: Model differences and new uses still need evaluation
en.text: MCP plus code mode looks promising to them, but implementations, model abilities and local-model support need testing. Armin also proposes code-defined workflows whose paths Jev can repeatedly select.

segments.text: So the problem that Armin identified recently with the release of Opus 5.5 was that it stopped using the
segments.zh: Armin 最近发现的问题是，Opus 5.5 发布后，

segments.text: edit tool and just basically uses bash for everything now.
segments.zh: 它不再使用 edit 工具了，基本上什么事都用 Bash。

segments.text: For, yeah, well, Python, why a bash?

segments.text: That might be token efficient.

segments.text: It might have some correctness issues like you identified.

segments.zh: 而从用户体验来说，你看着执行记录不断往下刷，

segments.text: So maybe, so I think that there are two
segments.zh: 我觉得这里有两个

segments.text: macro trends,

segments.text: I would say, that affect us too.
segments.zh: 它们也在影响我们。

segments.text: But I think like at least for the token max of the world, like why do we even care what the transcript is one?
segments.zh: 不过，对那些追求大量使用 token 的人来说，首先就是：为什么还要在意执行记录？

segments.text: It's like you only look at the end result.
segments.zh: 只看最终结果不就好了。

segments.text: And then the second, I think,
segments.zh: 第二个我觉得

segments.text: thing worth discussing is not everything is a coding agent.
segments.zh: 值得讨论的问题是，并不是所有 agent 都是编程 agent。

segments.text: And some things want to have more control.
segments.zh: 有些场景需要更强的控制。

segments.text: And like the less likely an agent is at using the things you want him to use,
segments.zh: agent 越不愿意使用你希望它使用的工具，

segments.text: the more control you're sort of giving away in one form or another.
segments.zh: 你就越是在以某种方式让出控制权。

segments.text: So maybe we start with like, what's the point of the transcript?
segments.zh: 那我们先聊聊：执行记录到底有什么用？

segments.text: Yeah, I mean, for me,
segments.zh: 对我来说，

segments.text: the transcript, the transcript with respect to seeing diffs and
segments.zh: 如果执行记录的作用是看 diff 之类的东西，

segments.text: so on is meaningless for me 99% of all the time.
segments.zh: 那在 99% 的时候，它对我都没意义。

segments.text: If I have more than one agent open, I'm not looking at all the transcripts flowing by.
segments.zh: 如果我同时开着多个 agent，我不会盯着所有执行记录看。

segments.text: That's a waste of my time.
segments.zh: 那是在浪费时间。

segments.text: I'm basically looking at the result, the artifacts, the file changes they made after they think they're done.
segments.zh: 我主要看结果，看它们自认为完成之后产出的东西和文件改动。

segments.text: And I do this in a proper IDE or editor with a nice diff tool where I have code
segments.zh: 而且我会在真正的 IDE 或编辑器里看，那里有好用的 diff 工具，

segments.text: navigation, might even be able to debug things like VS Code.
segments.zh: 能跳转代码，甚至能调试，比如 VS Code。

segments.text: And that seems to be a much better spend of my time than watching transcripts go by and seeing edit tool
segments.zh: 相比盯着执行记录、看 edit 工具调用，

segments.text: calls and kind of interfering when I see something stupid being generated or edited.
segments.zh: 一看到生成或修改了蠢东西就插手，我觉得这样更值得花时间。

segments.text: I think it's the same for me.
segments.zh: 我也差不多。

segments.text: I don't watch the transcript as it's doing except for a handful of cases,
segments.zh: 除了少数几种情况，我不会在它执行时盯着记录。

segments.text: one of which is if I ask it to, for instance, do something with a computer.
segments.zh: 一种情况是，我让它在计算机上做些操作。

segments.text: I'm not saying a computer use, but like, for instance,
segments.zh: 我不是指 computer use，而是比如说，

segments.text: configure CI or figure out some access to a
segments.zh: 配置 CI，或者搞清楚怎么访问

segments.text: remote service, like apply Pulumi things.
segments.zh: 远程服务，比如执行 Pulumi 的变更。

segments.text: Then I really care about what it's doing.
segments.zh: 这时候我就很关心它在做什么。

segments.text: But for the most part, the transcript to me doesn't have, at least when it implements stuff, I don't really care about it.
segments.zh: 但大多数时候，至少它在实现功能时，我并不太关心执行记录。

segments.text: I do, however, have the situation where I have a conversation with the agent about how to solve a particular problem.
segments.zh: 不过，我会和 agent 讨论具体问题该怎么解决。

segments.text: And in order for it to have a better understanding of what we're doing,
segments.zh: 为了让它更好地理解我们在做的事情，

segments.text: it is encouraged to read files, understand the code base and so forth.
segments.zh: 我会鼓励它读文件、理解代码库等等。

segments.text: And then you have this intermittent read some stuff, maybe do a POC, and then we discuss.
segments.zh: 于是过程就是：读一些东西，也许做个概念验证，然后我们继续讨论。

segments.text: And so most of the transcript now no longer collapses as nice in Pi as it used to because like all their,
segments.zh: 现在这些记录在 Pi 里不像以前那样能很好地折叠了，

segments.text: I mean, it probably already had a lot of like bash commands in there that already didn't compress all that well.
segments.zh: 虽然以前也有不少 Bash 命令，本来就不太好折叠。

segments.text: But now the inputs to those tool calls are humongous because they are all the writes now and they don't collapse.
segments.zh: 但现在这些工具调用的输入特别大，因为所有写入操作都放进去了，而且不会折叠。

segments.text: So the transcript now for me becomes harder to read when I do still want it just because all the
segments.zh: 所以在我确实想读记录的时候，它反而更难读了，

segments.text: verbosity and the ugliness of the tool calls in there.
segments.zh: 因为里面的工具调用又冗长又难看。

segments.text: Yeah.
segments.zh: 是的。

segments.text: I can see that something that touches a production system or even a staging system where you want to actually see individual
segments.zh: 我理解，如果操作涉及生产环境，甚至预发布环境，你确实会想看每条

segments.text: commands to judge whether something's going to go to shit real soon.
segments.zh: 命令，判断它是不是马上就要搞砸。

segments.text: That makes sense.
segments.zh: 这很合理。

segments.text: I don't know if there's a good solution to that.
segments.zh: 我不知道有没有好的解决办法。

segments.text: Like we looked at what other harnesses like Codex or Claude Code are doing.
segments.zh: 我们看过 Codex、Claude Code 等其他 harness 的做法。

segments.text: And I think you looked into Claude Code.
segments.zh: 你应该研究过 Claude Code。

segments.text: What's their solution here?
segments.zh: 它们是怎么解决的？

segments.text: So Claude Code on all the new models,
segments.zh: Claude Code 对所有新模型，

segments.text: which is Fable 5, 5.1 and Opus 5.5 uses,
segments.zh: 包括 Fable 5、5.1 和 Opus 5.5，都用了一个模式。

segments.text: I forgot the name, they had a really funny name for this, but it's basically a mode where two things are happening.
segments.zh: 名字我忘了，那个名字挺有意思的，但本质上它做两件事。

segments.text: One is it basically pushes with a prompt instruction, the agents would just use bash.
segments.zh: 第一，通过提示词指令，推动 agent 直接使用 Bash。

segments.text: So like they're reinforcing even the thing that sort of it does by hand, out of the box anyways.
segments.zh: 也就是说，模型本来默认就会这么做，它们还进一步强化了这种行为。

segments.text: But then what they are doing is they're snapshotting by writing into a separate Git work tree all the files that you're working on anyway.
segments.zh: 第二，它会把你正在处理的文件写入一个单独的 Git 工作树，保存快照。

segments.text: So in addition to the Git, it's not the user work tree in the traditional sense,
segments.zh: 在原有 Git 状态之外，它并不是传统意义上的用户工作树，

segments.text: but it writes into a separate index.
segments.zh: 而是写入一个单独的索引。

segments.text: So it maintains for each repo you're working on a separate index just for one agentic run.
segments.zh: 所以，对每个仓库，它都会为一次 agent 执行维护单独的索引。

segments.text: And then after and before each tool call,
segments.zh: 然后在每次工具调用前后，

segments.text: it compares the state of that local checkout to the work tree it had before.
segments.zh: 它会比较当前本地检出的状态和之前保存的工作树状态。

segments.text: And then it synthesizes a diff into the UI as if an edit tool call happened.
segments.zh: 再在界面里合成一个 diff，看起来像是发生了一次 edit 工具调用。

segments.text: So you can see the snapshot as it was taking place there.
segments.zh: 这样你就能看到当时发生的变化。

segments.text: And I think this is sort of, well, so I think that there are two kind of interesting things here.
segments.zh: 我觉得这里有两点挺有意思。

segments.text: One is that I actually sometimes do perform edits from the wrong working directory.
segments.zh: 首先，我有时确实会从另一个工作目录修改文件。

segments.text: And the reason for this is, for instance, we have pi, we have radius.
segments.zh: 比如我们有 Pi，也有 Radius。

segments.text: Every once in a while, I have to work on two things and actually do let it commit to the other thing.
segments.zh: 偶尔我需要同时处理两个项目，而且会让它向另一个项目提交。

segments.text: That will not work with the work tree approach anyway.
segments.zh: 这种工作树方案就处理不了这种情况。

segments.text: So like the moment you're outside of this place where you are, it doesn't work.
segments.zh: 只要越出了当前这个目录范围，就不管用了。

segments.text: The other thing is it's actually not super fast either because like you might have a lot of files in there,
segments.zh: 另一个问题是，它也不算特别快，因为里面可能有很多文件，

segments.text: which are at least not sufficiently tracked by Git so that you can very trivially make that work.
segments.zh: Git 对这些文件的跟踪情况，并不足以让这件事轻易完成。

segments.text: So it's a little bit unclear, I think, if it's a good trade-off.
segments.zh: 所以我不确定这个取舍是否划算。

segments.text: It also means in a way that what you generally consider to be the diff, which is against your commit,
segments.zh: 而且你通常理解的 diff，是相对于自己的提交来说的；

segments.text: and what then the coding agent thinks, which is against some sort of other index,
segments.zh: 编程 agent 理解的 diff，却是相对于另一个索引。

segments.text: like it's another form of indirection.
segments.zh: 这又多了一层间接关系。

segments.text: I'm actually not convinced that that's a particularly necessary trade-off.
segments.zh: 我不太相信这是一项特别有必要的取舍。

segments.text: I think at that point, just commit to Git and like make the diff experience versus the Git checkout work really well.
segments.zh: 到了这一步，我觉得还不如直接提交到 Git，把相对于 Git 检出状态的 diff 体验做好。

segments.text: So I don't know.
segments.zh: 所以，我也说不好。

segments.text: I actually, I think that there's another sort of like small wrinkle on it,
segments.zh: 我觉得还有个小问题，

segments.text: which is like if you actually do want to watch the transcript,
segments.zh: 就是假如你确实想看执行记录，

segments.text: like let's just assume you have a use case where you do want to watch the transcript.
segments.zh: 我们就假设你有这样的使用场景，

segments.text: You can't read that stuff anyways as it's happening.
segments.zh: 它执行时你其实也来不及读那些内容。

segments.text: So you could only ever read it once it's done, which like that's a little bit weird anyways.
segments.zh: 你只能等它做完再读，这本身也有点奇怪。

segments.text: So in a way, if you do want to read the transcript,
segments.zh: 所以，如果你真的想看执行记录，

segments.text: you probably want a summary of what it's about to do.
segments.zh: 你可能更想要的是：它接下来准备做什么的简短说明。

segments.text: I suppose.
segments.zh: 我想是这样。

segments.text: I guess the biggest takeaway here is we need better diff tools.
segments.zh: 最大的结论可能是：我们需要更好的 diff 工具。

segments.text: Yes.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.text: Yes.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.text: And I also like, like having tried a lot of diff tools now and sort of diff tools that also are Gentic integrated,
segments.zh: 我现在试过很多 diff 工具，也试过集成 agent 的 diff 工具，

segments.text: like friend of ours, the Tunk, then for modems, which I think is pretty neat,
segments.zh: 比如我们朋友做的那个工具［名称转写不清，待核］，我觉得挺不错。

segments.text: but it is also not quite what I want, I feel like.
segments.zh: 但它似乎也还不是我真正想要的。

segments.text: So there's definitely, at least for the coding use case, I think like the diff needs to work better.
segments.zh: 所以，至少对编程场景来说，diff 确实需要做得更好。

segments.text: It needs to support also like multi-stage commits, like in a PR.
segments.zh: 它还需要支持多阶段提交，比如一个 PR 中的多个阶段。

segments.text: Maybe not even multi-stage commits, but before you even commit,
segments.zh: 也不一定是多阶段提交，而是在正式提交之前，

segments.text: you want to take snapshots of your files at specific times.
segments.zh: 你就想在特定时刻给文件保存快照。

segments.text: I have this in my custom Pi review extension,
segments.zh: 我的自定义 Pi review 扩展就有这个功能，

segments.text: which is like a desktop UI using Daniel's Glimpse framework.
segments.zh: 它是一个用 Daniel 的 Glimpse 框架做的桌面界面。

segments.text: And I've used this for months, right?
segments.zh: 我已经用了好几个月了。

segments.text: And I just found I don't even need that anymore.
segments.zh: 但我发现，现在自己甚至不需要它了。

segments.text: Like I don't need these snapshots before I do a commit.
segments.zh: 我不需要在提交之前保存这些快照。

segments.text: I don't care so much anymore,
segments.zh: 已经没那么在意了，

segments.text: but mostly because I try to break down my stuff into very small commits in
segments.zh: 主要是因为我会把工作拆成非常小的提交，

segments.text: terms of lines of code.
segments.zh: 按代码行数来说是这样。

segments.text: But I guess that's not a scalable solution because some workflows might just result in a large diff,
segments.zh: 但这恐怕不是适用于所有情况的办法，因为有些工作流就是会产生很大的 diff，

segments.text: and you might want to have the snapshots.
segments.zh: 那你可能还是需要快照。

segments.text: Yeah, it's hard.
segments.zh: 是啊，很难。

segments.text: I mean, like obviously the goal should be make very small PRs.
segments.zh: 当然，目标应该是把 PR 做得很小。
